source.title: Double descent in the condition number
source.authors: T. Poggio; Gil Kur; Andrzej Banburski

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports double descent in condition numbers and compares it to test-error double descent, but it does not measure test error or test any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The two reported figures measure matrix condition numbers, not test error or risk, so they do not test the listed versions. The paper also mentions prior work on test-error double descent; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The note measures only condition numbers of random and kernel matrices, not test error or risk. It draws an analogy to test-error double descent and offers a possible mechanism (conditioning/stability), but reports no generalization results. So it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also argue that kernel matrices on high-dimensional i.i.d. data are well-conditioned without regularization, especially when n/d<1. They also say the condition number of K† behaves like test-error double descent for linear and kernel interpolants, and defer a stability theory to later work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures condition numbers of random matrices and a kernel matrix; it does not apply a test-error double-descent experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says the pattern is robust to choices of d and n at a fixed ratio; it also presents a radial-kernel example with σ = 5.

fits_no_version.finding: The condition number of an n×d Gaussian matrix, and of a radial kernel matrix on Gaussian data, peaks at d=n and is lower on either side.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For random matrices, conditioning (sensitivity to data error) shows a double-descent-shaped peak at the interpolation point d=n. This is proposed as a mechanism behind test-error double descent.

record.problems: The evidence relevant to the claim is an analogy based on condition number, not test error. The figures provide no tabulated values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: All; no deep networks or test error.
All; no test error versus sample size, although the condition number varies with n.
All; no risk is measured for any model class.
All; no label noise or regularization experiments. It only asserts that kernels need no regularization for conditioning.

record.verdict_notes: Short theoretical note relying on Marchenko–Pastur asymptotics. The figures give no uncertainty, and the sizes are only on the axes (n up to ~100 or ~140). It is relevant as a mechanistic analogy, not as a test of the claim.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test error in deep networks.
Effect of increasing training sample size on test error near interpolation.
Risk or test error across model classes as capacity grows.
A common effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations.
Noise, regularization, and multiple-descent effects on test error.
Whether effective parameter counting turns test-error double descent into a U-shaped curve.
